description: Every identifier or token the Bank Link backend hands to a client (or a client sends back), where it travels and the regular expression every side checks it with. A value in a URL PATH is made of letters, digits, `_` and `-` only; a value in a query or fragment may also hold RFC 3986 unreserved characters (`.`, `~`). The backend test mints each one through the real minting function and asserts its pattern; the fixtures are checked against it by the contract replay test. Front ends copy this file into their own tests.

formats.name: link_id
formats.description: The id of a link (a UUID).

formats.name: url_token
formats.description: The token of the hosted link address, `<hosted base>/bank/link/<token>`; the SDK also reads it from the fragment (`#t=`).

formats.name: client_token
formats.description: The token the customer's front end hands to the SDK.

formats.name: session_credential
formats.description: The credential of a person's session (`Authorization: BankLink <credential>`).

formats.name: resume_code
formats.description: The code the hosted page keeps across the bank trip. Its head is the link id (32 hex characters, the format minted once `MINT_LINK_BASED_RESUME_CODES` is on) or the session's number (digits, the format still minted before that). The dot is allowed: a resume code travels in a query, a fragment or a body, never in a path.

formats.name: frame_id
formats.description: The non-secret id of the embedded frame route `/bank/frame/<frame_id>`. It travels in a PATH, so it holds only letters, digits, `_` and `-`: `frm_<link id hex>-<expiry seconds>-<signature>`.

formats.name: state
formats.description: The `state` of a bank attempt: in the fragment of the Test Bank launcher address and in the query of the bank's return.

formats.name: link_ref
formats.description: The non-secret reference of a link in the return to the hosted page (`/bank/return?link_ref=`).

formats.name: manage_token
formats.description: The token of the person's own access page, `<hosted base>/bank/manage/<token>`: `mgu_<connection id hex>-<version>-<signature>`. It travels in a PATH.

formats.name: selection_token
formats.description: The token naming an offered account in the account choice.

formats.name: redirect_state
formats.description: The `state` the customer's `redirect_url` receives: a display-only signature.

formats.name: instance_id
formats.description: The id the hosted page or SDK generates once per page instance (a UUID); the backend binds a resume code to it.
formats.minted_by: the client (generated, never minted by the backend)

formats.name: error_code
formats.description: The `code` of an error body and of a link failure.

formats.name: institution_id
formats.description: The public id of a bank.

addresses.name: sdk_handoff
addresses.description: Full-page redirect handoff, step 1: the SDK sends the TOP window of the host page to the hosted page when the popup was blocked (or on a phone browser). Everything travels in the fragment, so no server log sees it; the hosted page removes the fragment from its address at once (history.replaceState) after reading it. The older `#t=<token>&resume=1&return=` form is gone: the token is never used, and `resume` is not a parameter (a page ignores it).

params.name: resume_code
params.description: The single-use code the frame obtained from `POST /v3/bank/link-session/resume-code/`.

params.name: instance_id
params.description: The id the SDK generated once for this page instance; the code is bound to it.

params.name: v
params.description: The protocol number of the SDK (the wire contract is additive only).

params.name: return
params.description: The host page's own address, a CANDIDATE only. The hosted page sends it to the backend as `return_to` and navigates only to the `return_url` the backend answers.

addresses.name: hosted_return
addresses.description: Full-page redirect handoff, step 3: after the bank the hosted page asks `POST /v3/bank/link-session/resume-code/` for a new code and sends the browser to the `return_url` of that answer (never to an address of its own) with `didit_resume=<code>` appended to the QUERY, before any hash. The host page's `resumeBankLink()` removes the parameter from the address and exchanges the code.

params.name: didit_resume
params.description: The single-use resume code for the step after the bank.
